**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examinations. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics, Paper 3 (0765/3), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2021. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Mathematical formulae booklet published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.
enonce_intro_markdown: The engine of a car works at constant rate of $15\ \mathrm{kW}$. The car travels along a straight level road with maximum speed of $120\ \mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$.
incertitudes: Question 7 (b) : le sujet imprime « constant speed of 40 km » (l'unité « h^-1 » est absente) ; lu comme 40 km h^-1, ce que confirme la partie (c) (« the speed is 40 km h^-1 »). Restitué entre crochets dans l'énoncé.

Question 7 : le sujet n'imprime pas de valeur de g ; retenue g = 9,8 m s^-2. Avec g = 9,8 : (b) 4,91 kW et (c) 27,2 s ; avec g = 10 : exactement 5 kW et environ 26,7 s (ces valeurs sont rappelées dans le corrigé).

Question 7 (c) : l'arrêt du moteur est lu sur la route inclinée de (b) (le texte enchaîne « If the engine of the car is shut off at the instant when the speed is 40 km h^-1 »), la résistance restant proportionnelle au carré de la vitesse. Sur route horizontale la voiture ne s'arrêterait jamais en temps fini (résistance kv^2 tendant vers 0), ce qui confirme cette lecture.

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the total resistance to the motion of the car.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** On the level road at maximum speed the acceleration is zero, so the driving force $F$ of the engine (forwards) equals the total resistance $R$ (backwards): $F = R$. The power of the engine is $P = Fv$.

Convert the speed: $\ v = 120\ \mathrm{km\,h^{-1}} = \dfrac{120\times 1000}{3600} = \dfrac{100}{3}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and $P = 15\,000\ \mathrm{W}$.

$$R = F = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{15\,000}{100/3} = 450\ \mathrm{N}$$

**The total resistance to the motion of the car at its maximum speed is $450\ \mathrm{N}$.**
themes: motion of a vehicle with resistance

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that the mass of the car is $1000\ \mathrm{kg}$ and that the resistance to motion is proportional to the square of the speed, find the rate at which the engine is working when the car is moving at constant speed of $40\ \mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$ [printed "40 km"; the unit $\mathrm{h^{-1}}$ is restored] up a road of inclination $\theta$, where $\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{25}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Resistance law.** The resistance is proportional to the square of the speed: $R = kv^2$. At the maximum speed $v = \dfrac{100}{3}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ it is $450\ \mathrm{N}$, so

$$k = \frac{450}{(100/3)^2} = \frac{450\times 9}{10\,000} = 0.405\ \mathrm{N\,s^2\,m^{-2}}$$

At $v_1 = 40\ \mathrm{km\,h^{-1}} = \dfrac{100}{9}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ the resistance is $R_1 = 0.405\left(\dfrac{100}{9}\right)^2 = 50\ \mathrm{N}$ (equivalently $450\times\left(\dfrac{40}{120}\right)^2 = 50\ \mathrm{N}$).

**Model.** The car moves up the road at constant speed, so the net force along the slope is zero. Positive direction: up the slope. Forces along the slope: the driving force $F_1$ up the slope, the resistance $R_1$ down the slope, and the component of the weight $mg\sin\theta$ down the slope, with $m = 1000\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\sin\theta = \dfrac1{25}$ and $g = 9.8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ (no value of $g$ is printed in this question).

$$F_1 = R_1 + mg\sin\theta = 50 + 1000\times 9.8\times\frac{1}{25} = 50 + 392 = 442\ \mathrm{N}$$

Rate of working of the engine:

$$P_1 = F_1 v_1 = 442\times\frac{100}{9} = \frac{44\,200}{9} \approx 4911\ \mathrm{W}$$

**The engine is working at about $4.91\ \mathrm{kW}$** ($4911\ \mathrm{W}$). (With $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ the driving force would be $450\ \mathrm{N}$ and the rate exactly $5\ \mathrm{kW}$.)
themes: motion of a vehicle with resistance

questions.enonce_markdown: If the engine of the car is shut off at the instant when the speed is $40\ \mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$, find the time the car takes to come to momentary rest.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** The engine is shut off while the car is still moving up the road of part (b), so the driving force is zero. (On a level road the car would never reach rest in a finite time, because the resistance $kv^2$ tends to $0$ as $v \to 0$; "momentary rest" therefore refers to the car on the slope.) Positive direction: up the slope. Forces along the slope: the resistance $kv^2$ and the weight component $mg\sin\theta$, both down the slope. With $W = mg\sin\theta = 392\ \mathrm{N}$ and $k = 0.405$:

$$m\frac{dv}{dt} = -\left(kv^2 + W\right) \;\Rightarrow\; 1000\,\frac{dv}{dt} = -\left(0.405\,v^2 + 392\right)$$

Separate the variables. The speed falls from $v_1 = \dfrac{100}{9}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ to $0$ in a time $t$:

$$t = 1000\int_0^{100/9}\frac{dv}{0.405\,v^2 + 392} = \frac{1000}{\sqrt{kW}}\tan^{-1}\!\left(v_1\sqrt{\frac{k}{W}}\right)$$

using $\displaystyle\int\frac{dv}{kv^2 + W} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{kW}}\tan^{-1}\!\left(v\sqrt{\tfrac{k}{W}}\right)$.

Numbers: $kW = 0.405\times 392 = 158.76 = 12.6^2$, so $\sqrt{kW} = 12.6$; and $v_1\sqrt{k/W} = \dfrac{100}{9}\times\dfrac{12.6}{392} = \dfrac{5}{14}$. Hence

$$t = \frac{1000}{12.6}\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{5}{14}\right) = \frac{5000}{63}\times 0.3430 \approx 27.2\ \mathrm{s}$$

**The car comes to momentary rest after about $27.2\ \mathrm{s}$** (with $g = 9.8$; with $g = 10$ the time would be about $26.7\ \mathrm{s}$).
themes: motion of a vehicle with resistance
